410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. Present party is neither CFPM nor food handler qualified. Provide food handler training for all participating employees. More knowledgeable staff can only help support safe food handling. 

(b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14(A) Cooling. The facility has bulk containers of food in the walk-in cooler that are cooked foods from previous days service. COOLING: KEEP ON COUNTER UNTIL PRODUCT IS 135F (USE PROBE THERMOMETER TO MONITOR TEMPERATURE). 
ONCE 135F, START ACTIVELY COOLING: 1) USE AN ICE BATH; 2) LEAVE UNCOVERED; 3) SMALLER PORTIONS/SHALLOW PANS; AND 4) PORTIONS IN THE FREEZER TO KNOCK DOWN HEAT BEFORE MOVING TO COOLER.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
findings.citation_text:

SCDPH has discussed the future operations of this facility and has the following solutions: 1) the facility will be upgraded to a Class I facility to insure multiple visits throughout the year; 2) the facility will be on a two week rotation of inspection by the director of EH and facility inspector to insure compliance with Code and that knowledge is being gained and applied; and 3) following a few months of follow-ups, the facility will be routinely visited by the SCDPH health educator to fill education gaps and to insure safe food handling between SCDPH visits. Inability to observe improvement will result in a suspension of permit until knowledge of proper food handling can be demonstrated. 
The food manager class is great education for all involved in the operations. Having multiple employees complete the training can only benefit Almadina operations. Please see that those employees that work any amount of time in the kitchen are at least food handler trained. But ideally food manager certificates should be obtained for employees. 


The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (O) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD safety, including FOOD allergy awareness, as it relates to their assigned duties. FOOD allergy awareness includes describing FOODS identified as MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS and the symptoms that a MAJOR FOOD ALLERGEN could cause in a sensitive individual who has an allergic reaction.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.14(A) Cooling. The facility has bulk containers of food in the walk-in cooler that are cooked foods from previous days service. The bulk containers show no signs of proper cooling: covered, large amounts, and no date marking. The chicken on the counter is temped at 90F which implies possible improper cooling and the obvious improper reheating/hot holding (see violation #21). 

COOLING: KEEP ON COUNTER UNTIL PRODUCT IS 135F (USE PROBE THERMOMETER TO MONITOR TEMPERATURE). 
ONCE 135F, START ACTIVELY COOLING: 1) USE AN ICE BATH; 2) LEAVE UNCOVERED; 3) SMALLER PORTIONS/SHALLOW PANS; AND 4) PORTIONS IN THE FREEZER TO KNOCK DOWN HEAT BEFORE MOVING TO COOLER. 

(A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. There are multiple items being held on counters and not in proper hot holding units. The facility has a hot holding display, a steam table, and a warmer available. None of these items are in-use today. During the inspection, chicken (cooked yesterday) was observed on the counter at 90ish F. The operator could not immediately explain why food from yesterday and just brought to the counter within the last 15 minutes was temping at 90F. See violation #20. The proper hot holding of foods was discussed as was the proper reheating behavior. A warmer was plugged-in and made available for use. 

HOLD FOODS AT 135F OR ABOVE ONCE COOKED.

REHEAT FROM COLD TEMPERATURE TO 165F WITHIN TWO HOURS. 

USE A PROBE THERMOMETER TO INSURE THIS PROCESS IS PROPERLY CONDUCTED. 
This hot holding practice will be monitored by SCDPH staff over the next few weeks to insure proper education to staff. 

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-401.11(A)(1) and (A)(3)-(8) Equipment, Clothes Washers and Dryers, and Storage Cabinets, Contamination Prevention. 

There is immediate concern over the lack of cleaning in this facility and the potential for cross-contamination. As a bare minimum, safe food handling should include a routine cleaning schedule that maintains surfaces clean. The facility does not have a single surface that is observed free of accumulated grease and soil. A follow-up for the following surfaces will be conducted in two weeks:
1) hood system - the hood has not been serviced since 2023. The baffles are observed coated with grease and ready to drip onto the food of the cook line - clean the baffles, the Ansul system, and service the hood.
2) Shelving in the walk-in cooler is coated with food debris and mold. The shelving should be removed and power washed to remove all access grease and soil. 
3) The dry storage shelving is observed coated with a dusting of powder from the various spices held on the shelves. The side brace is nearly yellow from powder from spices.
4) Fryer, flat top, steamer, and vertical broiler are observed thickly coated with accumulated grease. This appears to be a potential fire hazard. Clean the cooking surfaces.
5) Throughout the facility, in-use cooking utensils are not being removed every four hours for wash, rinse, and sanitizing. There were observed soiled knives and peelers under the prep cooler from previous days use. Discussed cleaning. This is one of the topics that will be covered in future educationals. Staff appeared to be unaware as to proper wash, rinse, and sanitizing practices. 
6) preparation cooler interior and exterior is observed soiled with accumulated food debris. 

Clean the aforementioned surfaces paying attention to maintaining these surfaces clean once the initial task is completed.  


(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, EQUIPMENT, a cabinet used for the storage of FOOD, or a cabinet that is used to store cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be located: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.
